run.question: My signup service is failing and users can't register. What should I check to debug this issue?

report.summary: Fetched runbook signup-service-debugging-runbook and carried it out with this Run's tools. The failing workload is in namespace app-162: Deployment signup-service (2 pods) and Deployment payments-service (1 pod), both created 2026-11-23T16:09:53Z in a namespace created the same second. All three pods have containers running with restartCount 0 but are Not Ready (ContainersNotReady). payments-service's own log states 'STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail' and 'Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key'; its /ready and /health return 503, so the payments-service Endpoints object holds only notReadyAddresses and no ready address. Both signup-service pods then log 'Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' and return 503 on GET /ready, and the signup-service Endpoints object likewise contains only notReadyAddresses — which is why users cannot reach the registration path. Service selectors and targetPort match the pod labels, no NetworkPolicy exists in app-162, no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff events exist and every event in the namespace is Normal (Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started, ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate), so crashlooping, scheduler, probe-unrelated network denial and Service misconfiguration are ruled out. Runbook steps 1, 2 and 4 were completed; step 3 (kubectl exec / port-forward curl from a signup pod) and step 5 (reading container env / the STRIPE key value) could not be carried out because no exec or port-forward tool exists and Secrets are unreadable — the deployment spec shows STRIPE_API_KEY comes from secretKeyRef payments-secrets/stripe-api-key, so the bad value is held by Secret payments-secrets and could not be read to verify. Prometheus and Jaeger were SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query in this Run, so no error-rate, latency or trace corroboration exists; the conclusion is partial for that reason and because the Secret value and its write time are unverified.

claims.text: Namespace app-162 contains exactly three workload pods: payments-service-6d94c44fdc-4vz42 (1 container) and signup-service pods signup-service-7c89545dc9-4qrns and signup-service-7c89545dc9-jhv79; each is owned by a ReplicaSet (payments-service-6d94c44fdc, signup-service-7c89545dc9) which is owned by Deployment payments-service and Deployment signup-service respectively.

payments-service container log at 16:09:55.781Z records 'ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail'; at 16:10:04.024Z it records 'ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key' with 'GET /health HTTP/1.1" 503', and its /ready requests at 16:09:59, 16:10:04 and 16:10:09 all return 503.

Deployment payments-service sets container env STRIPE_API_KEY from secretKeyRef name=payments-secrets key=stripe-api-key (and DATABASE_URL from secretKeyRef payments-secrets/database-url), with readinessProbe GET /ready:8080 periodSeconds 5 failureThreshold 3 and livenessProbe GET /health:8080 periodSeconds 10 failureThreshold 3.

Both signup-service pods log 'ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' every 5 seconds (16:09:59.885Z, 16:10:04.884Z, 16:10:09.884Z on pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-4qrns) immediately followed by 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503'; the same three error lines and 503s appear on pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-jhv79.

Endpoints object payments-service contains one subset with ports 8080 and only notReadyAddresses 10.244.0.37 (targetRef payments-service-6d94c44fdc-4vz42) and no ready addresses; Endpoints object signup-service likewise has only notReadyAddresses 10.244.0.35 and 10.244.0.36 (the two signup pods).

All three pods report container status running/started with restartCount 0, empty lastState, image python:3.11-slim (imageID sha256:896edfbcbf0c29ad15681617a8886cb9871b7f24c5fde4606114c8ee6bfe4c70), and Pod condition Ready=False with reason ContainersNotReady; Deployment status shows readyReplicas and availableReplicas unset for both deployments while spec.replicas are 1 (payments) and 2 (signup).

Service payments-service selects app=payments-service on port 8080 targetPort 8080 and Service signup-service selects app=signup-service on port 8080 targetPort 8080; the pods carry exactly those labels (app=payments-service / app=signup-service), so selector and port mapping match the running pods.
No NetworkPolicy objects exist in namespace app-162 (query returned zero items) and no ReplicationControllers exist cluster-wide.

Every event whose own timestamp falls in the window is Normal type: Deployment payments-service ScalingReplicaSet (scaled payments-service-6d94c44fdc 0->1), Deployment signup-service ScalingReplicaSet (scaled signup-service-7c89545dc9 0->2), ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate for the three pods, and Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started at 16:09:53-16:09:54Z; there is no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, Unhealthy or Failed event.

Namespace app-162 was created at 2026-11-23T16:09:53Z, and both deployments are generation 1 with observedGeneration 1, creationTimestamp 2026-11-23T16:09:53Z, last written by manager kubectl-client-side-apply at 16:09:53Z, each having a single ReplicaSet with replicas matching spec (1 and 2).

The only ConfigMap in namespace app-162 is kube-root-ca.crt (created 16:09:53Z); there is no application ConfigMap in that namespace, so no ConfigMap-held fault setting is visible for these workloads.

Primary chain: the STRIPE_API_KEY value taken from Secret payments-secrets key stripe-api-key is invalid, which makes payments-service answer 503 on /health and /ready; because the payments pod never becomes Ready its address stays only in notReadyAddresses, so kube-proxy on Service payments-service:8080 refuses connections, which is exactly the '[Errno 111] Connection refused' that signup-service logs; signup's own /ready check consequently returns 503, its two pods stay Not Ready and their addresses stay only in signup-service notReadyAddresses, so no user traffic reaches the signup path. The Secret value itself could not be read, so this remains a hypothesis about the value, not an observed value.

Secondary candidate: because payments-service livenessProbe GET /health:8080 has failureThreshold 3 and periodSeconds 10 while /health returns 503, the payments container is likely to be restarted by kubelet soon; at the sampled instant (16:10:38Z) restartCount was still 0 and lastState empty, so a restart had not yet happened and this is not observed impact.

Rejected: pod crashloop / OOM as cause. All three containers are running with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, and no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Failed event exists in the namespace, so none of the pods crashed or was evicted in the observed window.

Rejected: Service selector / targetPort misconfiguration or NetworkPolicy as cause of the connection refused. Selectors app=payments-service and app=signup-service match the running pods, targetPort 8080 equals the container PORT 8080 value, both Endpoints objects exist and are populated with the correct pod IPs (as notReadyAddresses), and namespace app-162 has no NetworkPolicy objects.

Runbook next steps for a human: correct the key in Secret payments-secrets (key stripe-api-key) with a valid Stripe key, then restart Deployment payments-service (kubectl rollout restart deployment/payments-service) and confirm payments /health and /ready return 200, that Endpoints payments-service gains a ready address, and that signup /ready returns 200 and Endpoints signup-service gains ready addresses; also confirm the referenced Secret keys exist before rollout so containers do not land in CreateContainerConfigError.

gaps: Prometheus was SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query in this Run (get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, list_prometheus_rules all returned status error SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate or latency series exists for app-162 workloads and no alert state could be read; these signals are unknown, not zero, and no latency trend is claimed.

Jaeger was also SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (traces_list_services, traces_search both errored), so no trace corroboration of the signup->payments call edge exists; additionally, the service-name list the tool exposes does not include signup-service or payments-service, so even a working backend would need those instrumented names verified.

Secret payments-secrets (and signup-secrets) cannot be read, so the actual stripe-api-key value and the database-url value are unverified; the runbook's step 5 (reading STRIPE/DATABASE env inside the container) also could not be carried out because no exec tool is available, and the runbook's step 3 (exec/curl from a signup pod, port-forward to payments) could not be executed for the same reason - Endpoints and the signup client error log were used instead.

It is unknown when the stripe-api-key value was written: the change_history integration is not available in this Run, and Secret metadata cannot be read; the namespace and both deployments were created at 2026-11-23T16:09:53Z, so no earlier state of this app in the cluster could be compared.

Application logs were only readable from 16:09:55Z to the 16:10:14Z window end (7 lines shown per pod, 4 and 14 later lines dropped as outside the window), so behaviour after 16:10:14Z - including whether payments was restarted by its failing liveness probe - is unknown.

signup-service's /health (liveness) result and the signup DATABASE_URL dependency were not verifiable in the sampled window: no signup /health request line appears in the logs read and no database error line was present, which is not proof the database path is healthy.
next_steps: Have an operator verify the Stripe key material referenced by Secret app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key and replace it with a valid key; the value itself cannot be read with these tools.

After the key is corrected, restart Deployment app-162/payments-service and watch payments /health and /ready responses plus the ready address on Endpoints app-162/payments-service, then confirm signup /ready returns 200 and Endpoints app-162/signup-service has a ready address.

Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access for this target so error-rate, latency and trace signals for signup-service and payments-service can be checked; without them no error-rate baseline or latency comparison is possible.

Consider gating signup readiness on a dependency that fails closed only for the registration path (or adding retry/circuit-breaker behaviour) so a payments outage does not remove every signup replica from the Service, as the runbook's prevention section also suggests.
Provide kubectl exec/port-forward equivalents so the runbook's step 3 (curl payments-service:8080/health from a signup pod) and step 5 (read in-container env) can actually be executed next time.
